speaker: Speaker
text: Welcome, everyone. Today is about keeping your software supply chain safe without slowing your team down.

speaker: Speaker
text: First, a quick picture. Every image you ship is built from many parts you did not write.

speaker: Speaker
text: Each of those parts is a place where something can go wrong.

speaker: Speaker
text: The goal is simple: know what is inside your image, and prove where it came from.

speaker: Speaker
text: Step one is a software bill of materials. Think of it as an ingredients list for your container.

speaker: Speaker
text: Step two is signing. A signature says this image came from our build system and nobody changed it.

speaker: Speaker
text: Step three is checking the signature before the image is allowed to run in the cluster.

speaker: Speaker
text: You can do all three inside the pipeline you already have. No extra meeting is needed.

speaker: Speaker
text: Here is the order I suggest: start with the ingredients list, then sign, then enforce.

speaker: Speaker
text: Enforce last, because if you block images on day one, people will look for a way around it.

speaker: Speaker
text: Start in warning mode. Watch what would have been blocked for a week.

speaker: Speaker
text: Then fix the noisy cases, and only then turn on blocking.

speaker: Speaker
text: Let's take a short pause for questions before the demo.

speaker: Speaker
text: In the demo I will sign one image, then try to run one that is not signed.

speaker: Speaker
text: Hello and welcome. This talk assumes you have never set up observability before.

speaker: Speaker
text: Observability means you can ask your system a new question without shipping new code.

speaker: Speaker
text: There are three kinds of signal: logs, metrics and traces.

speaker: Speaker
text: Logs tell you what happened. Metrics tell you how much. Traces tell you where the time went.

speaker: Speaker
text: If you only pick one to start, pick traces for a slow request. They show the whole path.

speaker: Speaker
text: OpenTelemetry gives you one way to collect all three, whatever tool you send them to.

speaker: Speaker
text: Let's look at one slow request together and find where it waited.

speaker: Speaker
text: Hi everyone. RBAC sounds scary, but the idea is small: who can do what, where.

speaker: Speaker
text: A Role is a list of allowed actions. A RoleBinding gives that list to someone.

speaker: Speaker
text: Start with the smallest list that lets the job work. Add more only when something fails.

speaker: Speaker
text: A ClusterRole works across the whole cluster, so be extra careful with those.

speaker: Speaker
text: Let's read one real-looking Role line by line, in plain words.

speaker: Host
text: Welcome to the open questions session on supply chain security.

speaker: Host
text: We will take written questions first, so people who prefer not to speak go first.

speaker: Panelist
text: A common question: do small teams need all of this? Start with the ingredients list. It is cheap.

speaker: Panelist
text: Another one: what if a signing key leaks? Rotate it, and keep the list of trusted keys short.
